slides.0.title: Regulation and Diploma/CMS Essays
slides.0.subtitle: EU categories, appellation comparison and answer frameworks
slides.1.title: EU category layers
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Layer 1: EU category
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Regulation (EU) 2019/787 defines Brandy/Weinbrand, Wine spirit, Grape marc spirit and Raisin spirit (see Level 1)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Layer 2: geographical indication
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Cognac, Armagnac, Brandy de Jerez, Deutscher Weinbrand, Grappa and others are protected geographical indications that add rules on raw material, distillation, ageing and origin on top of the EU category
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Layer 3: brand and age terms
slides.1.highlights.2.content: VS, VSOP, XO and similar terms are industry rules by appellation, not a single EU definition
slides.1.content: In an answer, state which layer applies before citing rules.
slides.2.title: Comparison table
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Cognac vs Armagnac
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Cognac: Charentais pot still, double distillation, at least 2 years in French oak. Armagnac: mostly single column distillation at about 52–60%, vintage labelling common
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Pisco (Peru)
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Single distillation, no water, no oak, three months in inert vessels; the opposite of Cognac, stressing raw-material character
slides.2.highlights.2.title: South Africa and Germany
slides.2.highlights.2.content: South African pot-still: 100% pot-still, casks of 340 L or less, at least 3 years, at least 38%. German Weinbrand: at least 38%, oak under 1,000 L for at least 12 months, sugar at most 20 g/L
slides.2.content: For comparison questions use five axes: raw material, distillation, ageing, additions, origin.
slides.3.title: Answer frameworks
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Explain-type questions
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Define → mechanism (e.g. still type and flavour) → example (e.g. Cognac vs Armagnac) → short conclusion
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Compare-type questions
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Choose three to five axes, compare both sides on each, and state the effect on style or price
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Commercial questions
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Fact (with year) → cause → impact on the supply chain → feasible response; never present speculation as fact
slides.3.content: These frameworks are study suggestions, not official marking criteria.
slides.4.title: Short-answer practice: question and marking points
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Question 1
slides.4.highlights.0.content: “Compare distillation in Cognac and Armagnac and explain how it affects style and ageing.” (about 250 words)
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Marking points for question 1
slides.4.highlights.1.content: ① Cognac: double distillation in Charentais pot stills to about 70–72%, with heads and tails cut both times → purer, more refined; ② Armagnac: mostly single continuous distillation, leaving the still at about 52–63% → more flavour compounds retained, characterful even when young; ③ ageing: Cognac at least 2 years in French oak, new casks then old; Armagnac in 400–420-litre casks, with rancio often appearing after about 20 years; ④ conclusion: the “purer” the distillate, the more it relies on oak and time for complexity
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Question 2
slides.4.highlights.2.content: “Assess the impact of the 2024–2025 changes in the Chinese market on the Cognac supply chain.” (can be answered orally in 2 minutes)
slides.4.highlights.3.title: Marking points for question 2
slides.4.highlights.3.content: ① facts: 2024 global export value −10.6%, China value −23.8%; from 5 July 2025 China imposed 27.7–34.9% anti-dumping duties on EU brandy, with some firms exempted through minimum-price undertakings; ② mechanism: falling exports → rising stocks → lower production and purchase prices → pressure on growers’ incomes; ③ the two sides of concentration: the big four have stock and marketing advantages, but dependence on one market magnifies policy risk; ④ conclusion: in the short term growers are hit hardest; in the long term markets must diversify and old, premium stocks be emphasised (state the years)
slides.4.content: What CMS orals and Diploma papers share: dated facts, causal mechanisms and a conclusion with a view.
What kind of terms are VS, VSOP and XO?
A. Industry rules by appellation, not one EU definition
The biggest ageing contrast between Peruvian pisco and Cognac?
A. Pisco avoids oak; Cognac requires it
20 g/L (the general EU brandy cap is 35 g/L).
A. 100% pot-still, at least 3 years, at least 38%
Suggested order for a commercial essay?
And never present speculation as fact.
